rv.q: Mallory and team have done a beautiful job of making Birch’s thorny play bloom, and I’d encourage any fan of serious Chicago-style acting to see this production before its limited run ends.
The Metal Shop Performance Lab and JunkHeart’s first full-length production is an unqualified triumph; that rare production where every element clicks into place perfectly.
Give yourself over completely to this powerful and thought-provoking, incredibly immersive theatrical experience and you’ll be a different person when you leave the theatre.
Anatomy of a Suicide is a bold work.
To my mind, this is an actor’s play, one for theater professionals, but not something the average ticket buyer would want to see.
Mallory has assembled a stellar ensemble, with a deep roster of some of our city's hardest working performers...
Anatomy of a Suicide is a challenging but worthwhile theatrical experience that encourages audiences to look more closely at mental health and family.
“Anatomy of a Suicide” by Alice Birch is in essence a good story, but it’s not told well.

cn.t: Critics praise this ambitious exploration of intergenerational trauma for its stellar performances and thought-provoking power, though some find Birch's fragmented storytelling more intellectually striking than emotionally gripping.
